dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product opens its pages the same way: the page's title, a sentence that says what the page is, a line of facts about it (a date, an author, a state, tags), the actions that belong to the whole page, and the way back up above them. It opens an article, a settings page, a record and a list of results with that head, a part of a page with a smaller one and its landing page with a larger one, and wants the title of each to be the heading a reader and a machine both find.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a page header reads: per size, the title's text style, the description's text style, the space between them and the space the head keeps below its last part; the eyebrow's text style, color and its distance from the title; the colors of the title, the description and the meta line; the description's longest line; the meta line's text style, the space above it, between its items, between its rows and between a glyph or an avatar and the text of one item, and the dot drawn between two items; the space above the actions and between them; the distance between the text and actions that stand beside it; the width of the head from which actions stand beside the title; the space below what stands above the title (breadcrumbs); and the line under the head.
rules: A page header is the head of a page's content: it says what the page is. Its title is the page's heading of level 1 — one per page or screen, never repeated in the app bar's title of the same screen, never an image. The head of a part of a page is the small size, whose title is a heading of level 2.
It stands in the content and scrolls with it. The bar at the top edge of the window is the app bar; the frame of regions is the app shell; a notice is a callout placed under the head.
Use medium for a page, small for a section of a page, large for the statement that opens a landing page. A size changes text styles and spaces only.
Write the eyebrow as a few words that say what the page belongs to (a category, a product, a version). The way up through a hierarchy is Breadcrumbs, or one Link back, in the breadcrumbs slot.
The description is one or two sentences. Long text belongs to the content below, as prose.

The meta line holds short facts about the page, each one item: a date (a time element on the web), an author's name with a small avatar, a reading time, a state as a Tag, a group of tags as one item. The page header draws the dot between two items; never write a separator of your own. Facts with names ("Category: Actions") are a description list below the head.

Actions are the product's Buttons and Links for the whole page, one to three, the main one filled. They stand beside the title while the head is wide and below the text while it is narrow; set actionsPlacement below to keep them under the text at every width.
The title wraps and is never cut: do not shorten a title to make it fit, and do not set a width on it.
The page header brings no fill. On a tinted band the product sets title.color, description.color, meta.color and eyebrow.color for that band.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a page title by hand.

gap.$description: The distance between the text (eyebrow, title, description, meta) and the actions while the actions stand beside it. Larger than any space inside the text, so the actions read as belonging to the whole head and not to one line of it.

padding-block-end.$description: The space the head keeps below its last part, inside its own box, per size: what follows a head starts further from it than two blocks of the content are from each other, by this much. Where the head draws its line (divider), the line is below this space, at the box's edge. The head brings no space above itself and no outer space at all.

container-width.$description: The width of the head itself — not of the window — from which it is wide: actions stand beside the title (PGH-10), and a large head draws its title at its own size (PGH-12). Below it the head is one column. It grows with enlarged text, so a head whose text was doubled goes to one column at twice this width.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows the same head in a wide page, in a pane beside a list and on a phone, and decides once how narrow a head may be before its actions leave the title's side: a product with long titles or many actions sets it wider.

gap.$description: The space below what stands above the title — Breadcrumbs, or a Link back — before the eyebrow or the title.

typescale.$description: The eyebrow's text style: the system's kicker, small and tracked wide. The page header draws it in capitals where the script has them (PGH-6); the token stores no text transform.

color.$description: The eyebrow: secondary content, quieter than the title it stands above.

gap.$description: Between the eyebrow and the title. Small, so the two read as one head.

typescale.$description: The title's text style, per size: a section's heading for small, the page's title for medium, the system's one statement size for large. A large head narrower than wide.container-width draws medium's (PGH-12).

color.$description: The title: the content color of the surface a page is drawn on.

typescale.$description: The description's text style, per size: the interface's running text under a section's title, the style for a lead and long reading under a page's and a landing page's.

color.$description: The description: secondary content, so that the title stays the first thing read. Held to 4.5:1 on every surface by the token invariants.

gap.$description: Between the title and the description, per size: a larger title stands further from the sentence under it.

measure.$description: The description's longest line, as a multiple of its own font size (ems): the number prose limits its text blocks to, so a description and the paragraph under it end at the same edge when they are set at the same size. The title is not limited by it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product limits how long a line of its lead sentence grows on a wide page, apart from how wide the head itself is, whose actions stand at the far edge.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A count of characters, not a distance: it scales with the description's text size by being multiplied by it, and no dial moves it.

typescale.$description: The text of the meta line: secondary text, one step under the interface's running text, at every size.

color.$description: The text of the meta line, where an item brings no color of its own (a Tag, a Link and an Avatar keep theirs).

gap.$description: The space above the meta line, below the description or, without one, the title.

item-gap.$description: Between two items on one row of the meta line. The separator is drawn in the middle of it.

row-gap.$description: Between two rows of the meta line where it wraps. Small, so that a wrapped line still reads as one line of facts.

gap.$description: Between a glyph or an avatar and the text of the same item: an author's picture and name, a calendar glyph and a date.

size.$description: The diameter of the dot drawn between two items on one row. Decorative: it is never at the start or the end of a row and is not exposed. A system that parts its meta items by space alone sets it to the scale's zero.

color.$description: The dot between two items: the color of the text it parts.

gap.$description: The space above the actions while they stand below the text.

item-gap.$description: Between two actions along their row, and between rows where they wrap.

color.$description: The line under the head, where the product asks for it: the system's one hairline color. Decorative.

thickness.$description: The width of the line under the head.
